newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates slip, but guilder slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates slip, but guilder slightly lower.

text.p: Dutch money rates slipped a little on Wednesday and dealers said rates were likely to go down further.
Foreign participants were mainly selling, while domestic market players were the main buyers.
"They are selling deposits up to three months," one dealer said of foreign clients, while another said most trade was in dollar-guilder swaps and other currencies versus the guilder.
"Volumes were back to normal levels," said one dealer adding trade had been sluggish for some days.
The guilder was trading at 112.16 per 100 marks versus 112.10 on Tuesday, but dealers said foreign investors were still showing confidence in the Dutch currency.
"The exchange rate is likely to stay near the current level," said one.
Two-month deposits shed four basis points to 2.74 percent bid and three-month paper was down six basis points at 2.76 percent bid. Call money rates were stable at 2.62 percent bid.
